test_meta.title: Percentage - Topic Test
test_meta.marking_scheme: +1 for each correct answer, 0 for unattempted, -0.25 for each incorrect answer (standard negative marking as used in CAT/XAT-style placement tests).
instructions: This test contains 25 questions on Percentage, of mixed difficulty (8 easy, 10 medium, 7 hard).
Total time allowed: 30 minutes. The timer starts as soon as you begin and auto-submits the test on expiry.
Each question carries 1 mark. There is a negative marking of 0.25 marks for every incorrect answer. Unattempted questions carry no penalty.
Do not use a calculator -- all questions are designed to be solvable through mental math and the shortcuts covered in the study material.
Use the question palette to navigate between questions and to identify unanswered questions before submitting.
Once submitted, the test cannot be resumed or re-attempted in the same session. Review the answer key and detailed solutions after submission.
Aim to spend no more than 70-75 seconds per question on average to finish with review time to spare.

questions.question: Find 16% of 350.
42 is what percent of 120?
Convert 11/40 to a percentage.
If 22% of a number is 66, find the number.
A price of Rs. 720 is increased by 15%. Find the new price.
A number decreases from 150 to 105. Find the percentage decrease.
Express 0.08 as a percentage.
A student scores 54 out of 90 marks. Find the percentage scored.
Two successive discounts of 25% and 10% are equivalent to a single discount of what percentage?
The price of rice rises by 10%. By what percent should consumption be reduced to keep expenditure unchanged? (to 2 decimal places)
In an election, the winner secured 58% of the votes polled and won by 3,200 votes. Find the total number of votes polled.
A population of 20,000 (as of 2 years ago) grows at 12% per annum. Find the current population.
A man's income rises from Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 27,500, and his expenditure of Rs. 20,000 rises by 5%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.
questions.explanation: Old savings = 5000. New expenditure = 21000. New income = 27500. New savings = 6500. % increase = (1500/5000)x100 = 30%.

questions.question: A's income is 15% less than B's. B's income is what percent more than A's? (to 2 decimal places)
55% of a number exceeds 2/5 of the number by 45. Find the number.
The passing percentage in an exam is 45%. A student scored 120 marks and failed by 15 marks. Find the maximum marks.
Two numbers are in the ratio 2:3. If the first is increased by 50% and the second by 20%, find the new ratio.
A shopkeeper allows a 12% discount on the marked price and gains 10%. If the cost price is Rs. 550, find the marked price.
A trader marks his goods 60% above cost price and gives successive discounts of 10% and 5%. Find his profit percentage.
A population of 40,000 grows by 15% in year 1, declines by 10% in year 2, and grows by 5% in year 3. Find the population after 3 years.
A salary of Rs. 30,000 is reduced by 10%, increased by 10%, then reduced by 10% again. Find the final salary.
In an election, 5% of the votes were invalid. The winner secured 52% of the valid votes and won by 2,280 votes. Find the total number of votes registered.
questions.explanation: Margin = 4% of valid votes = 2280 => valid votes = 57,000. Total registered = 57000/0.95 = 60,000.

questions.question: A's income is 35% more than B's, and B's income is 25% less than C's. If the total of A, B and C's incomes is Rs. 1,10,500, find B's income.
The length of a rectangle is increased by 25% and its breadth is decreased by 25%. Find the percentage change in its area.
A vessel has 60 litres of milk. 15 litres is removed and replaced with water; this is repeated two more times (3 operations total). Find the quantity of milk left.

score_bands.label: Excellent
score_bands.feedback: Percentage fundamentals and successive-change reasoning are placement-ready. Move to timed sectional mocks combining Percentage with Profit & Loss and Simple/Compound Interest.

score_bands.label: Good
score_bands.feedback: Core concepts are solid but revisit whichever difficulty band had the most errors -- typically successive-change or price-consumption questions. Redo the Hard solved examples before the next attempt.

score_bands.label: Needs Practice
score_bands.feedback: Revisit the Study Material formulas section, especially successive % change and the price-consumption relationship, then redo all 50 Solved Examples before reattempting.

score_bands.label: Foundational Gap
score_bands.feedback: Restart from the Study Material introduction and concepts sections. Focus on fraction-percentage conversion fluency before attempting timed tests.

metrics_to_report: Overall score (out of 25) and percentile against other attempts on this topic test
Accuracy % by difficulty band (Easy / Medium / Hard) to isolate where errors cluster
Average time per question vs the 72-second target, flagging questions that took over 120 seconds
Topic-tag-level breakdown (e.g. 'successive-change', 'price-consumption', 'election') to show which sub-skill needs the most reinforcement
Negative-marking impact: marks lost to incorrect attempts vs marks foregone by skipping
Comparison to the student's own previous Percentage topic test attempt (improvement/regression trend)
recommended_next_steps: If accuracy on Hard questions < 50%, revisit the 15 Hard Solved Examples and the Advanced Challenge set before reattempting the test
If average time per question > 90 seconds despite high accuracy, drill the Shortcut Methods section specifically for speed
If errors cluster on a specific tag (e.g. successive-change), redo all Practice Questions carrying that tag before moving to the next topic
